See also: Marche, marchè, and marché

Asturian

[edit]

Verb

[edit]

marche

  1. first/third-person singular present subjunctive of marchar

Franco-Provençal

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

marche (Old Dauphinois)

  1. alternative form of marchiê (“market”)

References

[edit]
  • Walther von Wartburg (1928–2002), “mercātus”, in Französisches Etymologisches Wörterbuch, volume 6/2: Mercatio–Mneme, page 1

French

[edit]
French Wikipedia has an article on:
marche
Wikipedia fr

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /maʁʃ/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Audio (Switzerland (Valais)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Brétigny-sur-Orge)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Lyon)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Somain)):(file)

Noun

[edit]

marche f (plural marches)

  1. march (formal, rhythmic way of walking)
  2. march (song in the genre of music written for marching)
  3. walk (distance walked)
  4. movement (of a vehicle)
  5. functioning
  6. step (step of a stair)
  7. marches (region near a border)

Derived terms

[edit]
  • en marche
  • fermer la marche
  • marche à suivre
  • marche arrière
  • marche de la mort
  • marche forcée
  • marche nordique
  • mettre en marche
  • ouvrir la marche

Related terms

[edit]
  • marcher

Descendants

[edit]
  • → Bulgarian: марш (marš)
  • → Egyptian Arabic: مرش (marš)
  • → English: mush
  • → Esperanto: marŝo
  • → German: Marsch
    • → Czech: marš
    • → Polish: marsz
    • → Russian: марш (marš)
  • → Macedonian: марш (marš)
  • → Serbo-Croatian:
    • Cyrillic script: марш
    • Latin script: marš
  • → Turkish: marş

Verb

[edit]

marche

  1. inflection of marcher:
    1. first/third-person singular present indicative/subjunctive
    2. second-person singular imperative

Further reading

[edit]
  • “marche”, in Trésor de la langue française informatisé [Digitized Treasury of the French Language], 2012

Anagrams

[edit]

Middle French

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • marce

Etymology

[edit]

From Old French marche, see below.

Noun

[edit]

marche f (plural marches)

  1. limit; boundary

Descendants

[edit]
  • French: marche
  • → Middle English: marche
    • English: march

References

[edit]
  • Frédéric Godefroy (1880–1902), “marche”, in Dictionnaire de l’ancienne langue française et de tous ses dialectes du IXe au XVe siècle […], Paris: F[riedrich] Vieweg; Émile Bouillon, →OCLC.

Norman

[edit]

Verb

[edit]

marche

  1. inflection of marchi:
    1. first/third-person singular present indicative/subjunctive
    2. second-person singular imperative

Old French

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • marchee, march, marce, merche

Etymology

[edit]

Either directly from Frankish *marku or through Latin marca, from Proto-Germanic *markō, from Proto-Indo-European *mórǵs (“edge, boundary”).

Noun

[edit]

marche oblique singular, f (oblique plural marches, nominative singular marche, nominative plural marches)

  1. limit; boundary

Descendants

[edit]
  • Middle French: marche, marce
    • French: marche
    • → Middle English: marche
      • English: march

References

[edit]
  • Frédéric Godefroy (1880–1902), “marche”, in Dictionnaire de l’ancienne langue française et de tous ses dialectes du IXe au XVe siècle […], Paris: F[riedrich] Vieweg; Émile Bouillon, →OCLC.
